description: Per-candidate backfill rows for #59 (track #50). Researched and run 2026-09-02. NO RECORD SECTION: Nee is a cardiologist and former ICU nurse who has held no public office, so there is nothing to populate a `record` array with, exactly as the issue says. Positions only, and no record entry was manufactured out of clinical work. Her Bluesky handle typo was found and fixed separately and is already merged as #106 (lisaneeforchiago -> lisaneeforchicago), so nothing in this PR touches the registry; the corrected handle is what was read here. The recency cutoff (2016-01-01, per the issue comment) excludes nothing: her candidacy launched 2026-07-07 and every source below is from 2026. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, AND WHAT DOES NOT EXIST. Her campaign site has NO platform or issues page - the nav is Meet Lisa / Updates / Donate, and /issues, /platform and /housing all return the 581645-byte homepage as a soft 404, the same shape as brewer's site. The homepage's only housing-adjacent line is 'affordability isn't a talking point but a reality' and /about is pure biography. Her Bluesky feed (13 posts, all read) is events, petition circulators, dogs and festivals - not one housing sentence - but it was the single most valuable thing searched, because two of these four rows were found ONLY there: it is where she links the Tribune op-ed and the Fran Spielman episode, and neither is listed on her own Updates page. All three podcast feeds in sources.json were pulled and grepped for her name: one hit, the Fran row. THE REAL DEAL Q&A DOES NOT EXIST FOR HER YET. That series is the questionnaire class #57 identified as the track's best source and it has published Brewer, Cardenas and Mendoza; as of 2026-09-02 therealdeal.com/chicago/feed/ carries no Nee entry and neither does a site search. So this is 'not yet published' rather than 'declined' - re-check it when the remaining issues run. No candidate forum appearance was found anywhere. WHAT IS EXCLUDED AND WHY. Seven launch-week pieces were fetched IN FULL and read, not skipped on assumption: the Sun-Times, WTTW, NBC5, ABC7 and FOX32 launch stories all reduce to the same press-release sentence about affordability with no housing content whatsoever, and the Tribune's launch profile is the clearest statement of the problem - it says in its own voice that 'she shared few details on the policy plans she would turn to on day one', and its only affordability passage is about health and food deserts. The CBS one-on-one with Dana Kozlov is a video page whose fetchable text is 1487 chars of boilerplate with no housing word in it. WTTW's July 29 Chicago Tonight FULL EPISODE is on YouTube (WE4fJG0wwcA, 23.7 min) and was deliberately not used: it carries other segments with other speakers, and the WTTW row below is that same interview written up by the outlet with the quotes already attributed, which is the safer source. ON THE OP-ED, a judgment call worth stating. The #97 ruling puts candidate-authored op-eds in scope, and this one is hers, but that same ruling excluded a cardenas op-ed for being about property taxes rather than housing. This one is about the city's population-and-revenue spiral with housing as one named component - 'Housing costs eat family budgets' and 'Chicago needs a real strategy to bring people back and keep them here: housing people can afford'. It was included because those are first-person housing sentences in a real outlet, and because an honest finding about this candidate depends on having searched her own writing and not only press coverage of her. ROW ORDER IS DELIBERATE: weakest source first, strongest last. write_stance is last-write-wins on summary/stance/mechanism wherever the #90 guard does not apply (it only refuses a mechanism-LESS proposal over a cell that already names one), and run_backfill processes rows in file order, so the row most likely to carry a real answer - WTTW, last - is staged last on purpose. That ordering turned out to be load-bearing; see the run log. RUN LOG 2026-09-02. All four rows ran locally from a residential IP; every URL fetched on the first attempt and nothing was blocked, so no --html-file was needed. Result: 4 housing statements across 2 sources, 3 stance cells, and ZERO mechanisms. WGN (YouTube, 12 min) returned 2 statements, both genuine first-person housing answers and better than a launch-day interview had any right to be - retaining existing affordability while building more, and building housing near CTA, which is the only zoning-reform content she has said anywhere. yt-dlp reached YouTube fine locally (#32 is a CI-runner-IP problem, not a local one). WTTW returned 2: expediting the permit process, and roughly 120,000 vacant places to fill. THE TRIBUNE OP-ED RETURNED ZERO HOUSING STATEMENTS, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED - it was run FOUR times (once live, three more into a scratch --data-dir) and returned 0 every time, because extraction is not reproducible and one run is not a measurement (CLAUDE.md). Her housing sentences in it are scene-setting for a fiscal argument, not positions. THE FRAN SPIELMAN EVIDENCE FILE WAS RUN AND THEN DELETED, and this is the main judgment call in the PR. The hour-long episode is the only long-form first-person source that exists for her, and it produced 4 statements of which NONE is about housing: (0) 'What you can't do is put it back on the taxpayer' - pensions, and CLAUDE.md's own rule for this candidate is that a property-tax-only quote does not count as housing; (1) 'grow the tax base... bring people into the city' - the reviewer itself noted 'she doesn't explicitly mention housing in this specific quote'; (2) small and medium-sized businesses and their switching costs - nothing; (3) the mayor leaving the CTA, the CHA and the health commissioner posts vacant - a governance criticism that names the CHA in a list. The episode's own RSS description is pure biography, which is what a genuinely 0-housing hour looks like. Two of those four had reached the matrix as cells before the deletion and both were wrong in the way this track keeps getting burned by: property-taxes-tif rendered as 'opposes', which on a housing matrix reads as opposing relief from property-tax burden - the exact inversion #57 exists to prevent, except no guard fired because there was no prior cell to invert; and public-housing-cha rendered a cell implying she has a CHA position. THE REVIEWER INDEPENDENTLY FLAGGED that second one (its summary said 'CHA commissioner', conflating two of the three vacancies she listed), which is the same two-model agreement that justified deleting brewer's statement #9. Deleting the whole file rather than leaving the statements in uncited was deliberate and was checked rather than assumed: site/src/pages/feed.astro renders every evidence file's housing-statement TOPICS as tags on the public feed, and buildCandidateProfile puts every evidence file with a statement for the candidate on her profile timeline - neither needs a citation - so an uncited statement publishes 'Property taxes / TIF' against her name anyway. Uncited is not inert. The fran#1 citation was also dropped from the affordable-housing-funding cell, which now cites WGN#0 and WTTW#1. A SIXTH WAY write_stance QUIETLY DEGRADES A CELL, caught live here by #98's new before/after rendering, which is the first time that rendering has run on real data. The Fran row moved affordable-housing-funding from 'supports' ('build additional affordable housing') to 'no-position' ('grow the tax base... relates to housing affordability indirectly') and it LANDED. #57 only guards the supporting labels against 'opposes'; #90 only guards a named mechanism against a mechanism-less proposal. Neither covers a supports -> no-position downgrade, and both sides here had mechanism null. Only the deliberate row ordering above put WTTW last and restored it. Not fixed in this PR - it is a code change with its own test. ZERO MECHANISMS IS THE FINDING, and unlike giannoulias it is not a sourcing failure: there is no platform page to have missed, the podcast feeds were grepped, the one long interview was run, and her own op-ed was run four times. She names no instrument anywhere. 'Expedite the permit process' is the borderline rule's own example of a null ('streamline permitting' is null, 'cut permit review to 30 days' is a mechanism), and '120,000 vacant places' is a count of the problem rather than an instrument for it. Three cells with an honest null beats padding, which is what the issue asked for.
